surfaces.part: blue front panel with white Korean lettering

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a tall rectangle, 14 px wide from row 1 to row 30. Rows 1-5 form a pale band (L about 231-237) across the full width. It ends in a slightly darker front-edge line at row 5 (L=202), and row 6 is a dark line (L=17) that works as eave shadow. That fits evidence (a) for a top surface, although the band is only 5 rows and could also be read as a pale header panel. Below it, rows 7-27 are the blue front face with white lettering, and rows 28-30 are a dark base. No receding side face is drawn. The top is shallow, but it has an edge line and a shadow row, so it is not just a rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical sign: a pale panel with a dark blue border and Korean text, drawn at the same scale. Its 9 visible tones per tile fall between bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12), and well under vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the panel is not a flat fill, and the text and border break it up. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue rather than black, which matches the references. Shading is about 4 steps (light face, mid, shadow side, dark border) against roughly 5 on the references. The panel is a simple, thin object with little grain or per-pixel detail, so it reads a bit flatter than kiosk-a and vending-a. It is acceptable next to the bus shelter. Overall it is slightly lower in richness but within the range of shipped art for this kind, and it does not look like a sticker.
